title: Why is Brasília shaped like an airplane?
hook: Lúcio Costa didn’t draw an airplane. He drew a cross.
summary: Lúcio Costa’s Plano Piloto began as two crossing axes, one bent to fit the land; the airplane is a popular reading.

cardBlocks.text: From above, Brasília’s Plano Piloto looks like an airplane: a straight body and two curved wings. But the planner Lúcio Costa did not start from that image. In the report that won the competition for the new capital in 1957, he wrote that the plan came from two axes crossing at a right angle, the sign of the cross itself.

To fit the terrain, one axis was bent into a curve. That gave the Monumental Axis, with the Esplanade of the Ministries, and the curved Road Axis, with the North and South Wings. Hence the airplane, an image that stuck. But it is a popular reading: Costa himself preferred to compare the plan to a butterfly.
Brasília began as a cross of two axes; the airplane is a popular reading, not Lúcio Costa’s idea.

deepDiveBlocks.text: Costa handed in only a simple sketch and a written report, far less than the other entrants. Even so, out of 26 entries, the jury chose his, number 22.

In 1987, Brasília was added to UNESCO’s World Heritage List. What is protected is Costa’s urban plan, not Oscar Niemeyer’s buildings, which have their own laws. The plan works on four scales: monumental, residential, social and bucolic.
The architect Léon Pressouyre, who reported on Brasília’s bid for UNESCO, saw in it "a giant bird flying towards the southeast".

sobreviveu a ideia de um Eixo Monumental, como corpo desse avião, e de um Eixo Rodoviário, como suas asas, divididas em Asa Norte e Asa Sul.

claims.text: Lúcio Costa won the competition for the Plano Piloto in 1957.

support.excerpt: O Plano Piloto da cidade de Brasília, no Distrito Federal, foi projetado por Lucio Costa, vencedor do concurso, em 1957, para o projeto urbanístico da Nova Capital.

claims.text: In his competition report, Costa wrote that the plan came from two axes crossing at a right angle, "the sign of the cross itself".

support.excerpt: o urbanista explicou que o traçado "nasceu do gesto primário de quem assinala um lugar ou dele toma posse: dois eixos cruzando-se em ângulo reto, ou seja, o próprio sinal da cruz".
No relatório que escreveu para justificar sua proposta, o arquiteto e urbanista define Brasília como um “sinal da cruz”.

claims.text: To fit the terrain, one of the axes was bent into a curve.

Laid out along a monumental east-west axis, crossed by a north-south axis curved to follow the topography as a transportation thoroughfare

claims.text: The Monumental Axis holds the Esplanade of the Ministries; the North and South Wings run along the Road Axis.
